The same run measured the draw record area at 60 bytes: the published cache sits (sequences+1)*12 = 192 into the 252-byte allocation, so 7 records fit and r14's 9-record tree wrote past the end of it. r16 reads the map fields from hooks::gauge_instance() and prints four array entries, the length main+0x5456e4 indexes with. r14 (NRO 6e061c70779cfb3a306835030256012e50dd19fdbeeae36d4d4635c331d35b8d) remains the failed insertion run: the rectangle the game built from the mask had left/top 0 0 in all 2512 lines, never the requested 110,32, and the quest-end crash is main+0x5456e4 indexing the instance's array with main+0xa47d2c's node count + 1. Not approved for distribution; r16 runtime NOT RUN; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.

limitations: r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.
r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in both sessions that logged it).
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.
